findings.title: New abstract order() method breaks all external CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: The PR adds `int order();` as an abstract method to the public `CryptoProvider` interface in keycloak-common. Any third-party or downstream implementation of this interface (which is the documented SPI for plugging in custom crypto providers) will now fail to compile, and pre-compiled implementations will throw AbstractMethodError when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` during sorting. Since the method is only needed for tie-breaking, it should be declared as a `default int order() { return 0; }` to remain backward compatible.

findings.title: Multiple full providers with equal order() are now silently picked arbitrarily instead of failing
findings.body: Previously, having more than one CryptoProvider on the classpath threw an IllegalStateException ('Multiple crypto providers loaded...'), which caught misconfigurations such as having both the default (BC) and the FIPS1402 provider present. After this change, the code sorts by order() and silently uses the first. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return order() == 200, so if two of them end up on the classpath (e.g. both BC non-FIPS and BC-FIPS jars present), the selected provider depends on ServiceLoader iteration order, which is unspecified. This can silently run the server with the wrong crypto backend (e.g. non-FIPS instead of FIPS), where previously it failed fast. The equal-order case among 'real' providers should still be treated as an error.

findings.title: Dead code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two encoder results discarded
findings.body: In `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`, lines 114-115 call `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger)` and discard the results; the actual encoding is redone below in the `writeDerSeq(...)` call. The discarded calls are confusing leftovers and should be removed (they have no effect other than allocating unused objects).

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the default keystore JCA provider, not a BouncyCastle provider
findings.body: `getBouncyCastleProvider()` is documented in CryptoProvider as returning the BouncyCastle security provider (FIPS or non-FIPS). This implementation returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is whatever JCA provider implements the default keystore type (e.g. SUN). Any code path that calls this expecting BouncyCastle algorithms (e.g. BouncyIntegration) will get the wrong provider. It would be safer to throw UnsupportedOperationException like the other unsupported methods, or return null explicitly.
